byteOrder must be Exiv2::littleEndian or Exiv2::bigEndian.

functions.name: Exiv2::DataBuf::write_uint64
functions.signature: void Exiv2::DataBuf::write_uint64(size_t offset, uint64_t x, Exiv2::ByteOrder byteOrder)
functions.description: Writes a 64-bit unsigned integer at the given offset using the specified byte order.
requirements: offset + 8 must be less than or equal to size().
byteOrder must be Exiv2::littleEndian or Exiv2::bigEndian.
The buffer must be allocated to at least offset+8 bytes prior to calling.

functions.name: Exiv2::DataBuf::cmpBytes
functions.signature: int Exiv2::DataBuf::cmpBytes(size_t offset, const void* buf, size_t bufsize) const
functions.description: Compares bufsize bytes starting at the given offset with an external buffer, equivalent to memcmp(&pData_[offset], buf, bufsize). Returns <0, 0, or >0 like memcmp.
requirements: offset + bufsize must be less than or equal to size().
buf must be non-null if bufsize > 0 and point to at least bufsize readable bytes.

functions.name: Exiv2::DataBuf::data
functions.description: Returns a mutable pointer to the underlying data at the given offset.
requirements: offset must be less than or equal to size(). If offset == size(), the returned pointer may be valid for zero-length ranges only.
Any modification to the buffer capacity (alloc/resize/reset) invalidates previously returned pointers.

functions.name: Exiv2::DataBuf::c_data
functions.description: Returns a const pointer to the underlying data at the given offset.
requirements: offset must be less than or equal to size(). If offset == size(), the returned pointer may be valid for zero-length ranges only.
Pointer validity is invalidated by non-const operations that reallocate or reset the buffer.

functions.name: Exiv2::DataBuf::c_str
functions.description: Returns a const C-style string pointer starting at the given offset into the buffer.
requirements: offset must be less than or equal to size().
The buffer region starting at offset must be null-terminated before any C-string operations are performed by the caller; the function does not append a terminator.
Pointer validity may be invalidated by subsequent non-const operations on the DataBuf.

functions.name: Exiv2::makeSlice
functions.signature: ExIV2API Slice<Exiv2::byte*> Exiv2::makeSlice(Exiv2::DataBuf& buf, size_t begin, size_t end)
functions.description: Creates a mutable Slice over the DataBuf’s data in the byte range [begin, end). Intended to provide a bounds-checked, slice-like view into the buffer.
requirements: begin must be less than end.
begin and end must be less than or equal to LONG_MAX (end > LONG_MAX throws std::invalid_argument).
begin and end must be within buf.size(); otherwise Slice construction may throw per Slice’s constructor semantics.
May throw exceptions propagated from Slice construction.

functions.name: Exiv2::makeSlice
functions.signature: ExIV2API Slice<const Exiv2::byte*> Exiv2::makeSlice(const Exiv2::DataBuf& buf, size_t begin, size_t end)
functions.description: Creates an immutable Slice over the DataBuf’s data in the byte range [begin, end).
requirements: begin must be less than end.
begin and end must be less than or equal to LONG_MAX (end > LONG_MAX throws std::invalid_argument).
begin and end must be within buf.size(); otherwise Slice construction may throw per Slice’s constructor semantics.
May throw exceptions propagated from Slice construction.

functions.name: Exiv2::getUShort
functions.signature: Exiv2API uint16_t Exiv2::getUShort(const Exiv2::byte* buf, Exiv2::ByteOrder byteOrder)
functions.description: Reads a 2-byte unsigned short from a raw buffer with the specified byte order.
requirements: buf must be non-null and point to at least 2 readable bytes.
byteOrder must be Exiv2::littleEndian or Exiv2::bigEndian; Exiv2::invalidByteOrder behavior is unspecified.

functions.name: Exiv2::getULong
functions.signature: Exiv2API uint32_t Exiv2::getULong(const Exiv2::byte* buf, Exiv2::ByteOrder byteOrder)
functions.description: Reads a 4-byte unsigned integer from a raw buffer with the specified byte order.
requirements: buf must be non-null and point to at least 4 readable bytes.
byteOrder must be Exiv2::littleEndian or Exiv2::bigEndian.

functions.name: Exiv2::getULongLong
functions.signature: Exiv2API uint64_t Exiv2::getULongLong(const Exiv2::byte* buf, Exiv2::ByteOrder byteOrder)
functions.description: Reads an 8-byte unsigned integer from a raw buffer with the specified byte order.
requirements: buf must be non-null and point to at least 8 readable bytes.
byteOrder must be Exiv2::littleEndian or Exiv2::bigEndian.

functions.name: Exiv2::getURational
functions.signature: Exiv2API Exiv2::URational Exiv2::getURational(const Exiv2::byte* buf, Exiv2::ByteOrder byteOrder)
functions.description: Reads an 8-byte unsigned rational value (two 32-bit unsigned integers: numerator and denominator) from a raw buffer using the specified byte order.
requirements: buf must be non-null and point to at least 8 readable bytes.
byteOrder must be Exiv2::littleEndian or Exiv2::bigEndian.

functions.name: Exiv2::getShort
functions.signature: Exiv2API int16_t Exiv2::getShort(const Exiv2::byte* buf, Exiv2::ByteOrder byteOrder)
functions.description: Reads a 2-byte signed short from a raw buffer with the specified byte order.
requirements: buf must be non-null and point to at least 2 readable bytes.
byteOrder must be Exiv2::littleEndian or Exiv2::bigEndian.

functions.name: Exiv2::getLong
functions.signature: Exiv2API int32_t Exiv2::getLong(const Exiv2::byte* buf, Exiv2::ByteOrder byteOrder)
functions.description: Reads a 4-byte signed long (32-bit) from a raw buffer with the specified byte order.
requirements: buf must be non-null and point to at least 4 readable bytes.
byteOrder must be Exiv2::littleEndian or Exiv2::bigEndian.

functions.name: Exiv2::getRational
functions.signature: Exiv2API Exiv2::Rational Exiv2::getRational(const Exiv2::byte* buf, Exiv2::ByteOrder byteOrder)
functions.description: Reads an 8-byte signed rational value (two 32-bit signed integers: numerator and denominator) from a raw buffer using the specified byte order.
requirements: buf must be non-null and point to at least 8 readable bytes.
byteOrder must be Exiv2::littleEndian or Exiv2::bigEndian.

functions.name: Exiv2::getFloat
functions.signature: Exiv2API float Exiv2::getFloat(const Exiv2::byte* buf, Exiv2::ByteOrder byteOrder)
functions.description: Reads a 4-byte IEEE-754 single-precision float from a raw buffer using the specified byte order.
requirements: buf must be non-null and point to at least 4 readable bytes.
byteOrder must be Exiv2::littleEndian or Exiv2::bigEndian.

functions.name: Exiv2::getDouble
functions.signature: Exiv2API double Exiv2::getDouble(const Exiv2::byte* buf, Exiv2::ByteOrder byteOrder)
functions.description: Reads an 8-byte IEEE-754 double-precision float from a raw buffer using the specified byte order.
requirements: buf must be non-null and point to at least 8 readable bytes.
byteOrder must be Exiv2::littleEndian or Exiv2::bigEndian.

functions.name: Exiv2::operator<<
functions.signature: Exiv2API std::ostream& Exiv2::operator<<(std::ostream& os, const Exiv2::Rational& r)
functions.description: Stream output operator for a signed Rational (numerator, denominator). Formats the value to the provided ostream. Exact textual format is library-defined.
requirements: os must be a valid output stream; stream error state will affect output.
r is provided by const reference; no special constraints.

functions.name: Exiv2::operator<<
functions.signature: Exiv2API std::ostream& Exiv2::operator<<(std::ostream& os, const Exiv2::URational& r)
functions.description: Stream output operator for an unsigned URational (numerator, denominator). Formats the value to the provided ostream. Exact textual format is library-defined.
requirements: os must be a valid output stream; stream error state will affect output.

functions.name: Exiv2::operator>>
functions.signature: Exiv2API std::istream& Exiv2::operator>>(std::istream& is, Exiv2::Rational& r)
functions.description: Stream input operator for a signed Rational. Parses a Rational from the input stream. Accepted textual formats are library-defined.
requirements: is must be a valid input stream; operator reads characters and sets failbit on parse failure.
r is assigned only if parsing succeeds; exact behavior on partial reads follows iostream conventions.

functions.name: Exiv2::operator>>
functions.signature: Exiv2API std::istream& Exiv2::operator>>(std::istream& is, Exiv2::URational& r)
functions.description: Stream input operator for an unsigned URational. Parses a URational from the input stream. Accepted textual formats are library-defined.
requirements: is must be a valid input stream; operator reads characters and sets failbit on parse failure.
r is assigned only if parsing succeeds; exact behavior on partial reads follows iostream conventions.

functions.name: Exiv2::us2Data
functions.signature: Exiv2API size_t Exiv2::us2Data(Exiv2::byte* buf, uint16_t s, Exiv2::ByteOrder byteOrder)
functions.description: Converts an unsigned short to its byte representation using the specified byte order and writes it to buf. Returns the number of bytes written (2).
requirements: buf must be non-null and point to at least 2 writable bytes.
byteOrder must be Exiv2::littleEndian or Exiv2::bigEndian.

functions.name: Exiv2::ul2Data
functions.signature: Exiv2API size_t Exiv2::ul2Data(Exiv2::byte* buf, uint32_t l, Exiv2::ByteOrder byteOrder)
functions.description: Converts a 32-bit unsigned integer to its byte representation using the specified byte order and writes it to buf. Returns the number of bytes written (4).
requirements: buf must be non-null and point to at least 4 writable bytes.
byteOrder must be Exiv2::littleEndian or Exiv2::bigEndian.

functions.name: Exiv2::ull2Data
functions.signature: Exiv2API size_t Exiv2::ull2Data(Exiv2::byte* buf, uint64_t l, Exiv2::ByteOrder byteOrder)
functions.description: Converts a 64-bit unsigned integer to its byte representation using the specified byte order and writes it to buf. Returns the number of bytes written (8).
requirements: buf must be non-null and point to at least 8 writable bytes.
byteOrder must be Exiv2::littleEndian or Exiv2::bigEndian.

functions.name: Exiv2::ur2Data
functions.signature: Exiv2API size_t Exiv2::ur2Data(Exiv2::byte* buf, Exiv2::URational l, Exiv2::ByteOrder byteOrder)
functions.description: Converts an unsigned rational (two 32-bit unsigned integers) to its byte representation using the specified byte order and writes it to buf. Returns the number of bytes written (8).
requirements: buf must be non-null and point to at least 8 writable bytes.
byteOrder must be Exiv2::littleEndian or Exiv2::bigEndian.

functions.name: Exiv2::s2Data
functions.signature: Exiv2API size_t Exiv2::s2Data(Exiv2::byte* buf, int16_t s, Exiv2::ByteOrder byteOrder)
functions.description: Converts a 16-bit signed integer to its byte representation using the specified byte order and writes it to buf. Returns the number of bytes written (2).
requirements: buf must be non-null and point to at least 2 writable bytes.
byteOrder must be Exiv2::littleEndian or Exiv2::bigEndian.

functions.name: Exiv2::l2Data
functions.signature: Exiv2API size_t Exiv2::l2Data(Exiv2::byte* buf, int32_t l, Exiv2::ByteOrder byteOrder)
functions.description: Converts a 32-bit signed integer to its byte representation using the specified byte order and writes it to buf. Returns the number of bytes written (4).
requirements: buf must be non-null and point to at least 4 writable bytes.
byteOrder must be Exiv2::littleEndian or Exiv2::bigEndian.

functions.name: Exiv2::r2Data
functions.signature: Exiv2API size_t Exiv2::r2Data(Exiv2::byte* buf, Exiv2::Rational l, Exiv2::ByteOrder byteOrder)
functions.description: Converts a signed rational (two 32-bit signed integers) to its byte representation using the specified byte order and writes it to buf. Returns the number of bytes written (8).
requirements: buf must be non-null and point to at least 8 writable bytes.
byteOrder must be Exiv2::littleEndian or Exiv2::bigEndian.

functions.name: Exiv2::f2Data
functions.signature: Exiv2API size_t Exiv2::f2Data(Exiv2::byte* buf, float f, Exiv2::ByteOrder byteOrder)
functions.description: Converts a 4-byte IEEE-754 single-precision float to its byte representation using the specified byte order and writes it to buf. Returns the number of bytes written (4).
requirements: buf must be non-null and point to at least 4 writable bytes.
byteOrder must be Exiv2::littleEndian or Exiv2::bigEndian.

functions.name: Exiv2::d2Data
functions.signature: Exiv2API size_t Exiv2::d2Data(Exiv2::byte* buf, double d, Exiv2::ByteOrder byteOrder)
functions.description: Converts an 8-byte IEEE-754 double-precision float to its byte representation using the specified byte order and writes it to buf. Returns the number of bytes written (8).
requirements: buf must be non-null and point to at least 8 writable bytes.
byteOrder must be Exiv2::littleEndian or Exiv2::bigEndian.

functions.name: Exiv2::hexdump
functions.signature: Exiv2API void Exiv2::hexdump(std::ostream& os, const Exiv2::byte* buf, size_t len, size_t offset = 0)
functions.description: Prints len bytes from buf to the output stream in hex and ASCII format, prefixing each line with the logical position (offset + index). Useful for debugging binary buffers.
requirements: os must be a valid output stream.
buf must be non-null if len > 0 and point to at least len readable bytes.
offset is used only for display; it does not affect reading from buf.

functions.name: Exiv2::isHex
functions.signature: Exiv2API bool Exiv2::isHex(const std::string& str, size_t size = 0, const std::string& prefix = "")
functions.description: Returns true if str starts with prefix and is followed by exactly size hexadecimal digits (0-9, a-f, A-F). If size is 0, any number of hex digits is allowed and all are checked.
requirements: prefix comparison is case-sensitive.
If size > 0, str must contain at least prefix.size() + size characters to return true.

functions.name: Exiv2::exifTime
functions.signature: Exiv2API int Exiv2::exifTime(const char* buf, tm* tm)
functions.description: Parses a string in the format "%Y:%m:%d %H:%M:%S" (e.g., "2007:05:24 12:31:55") into a broken-down time (tm). Returns 0 on success, 1 on failure.
requirements: buf must be a non-null, null-terminated C-string in the exact format "%Y:%m:%d %H:%M:%S".
tm must be a non-null pointer to a tm structure to receive the result.

functions.name: Exiv2::exvGettext
functions.signature: Exiv2API const char* Exiv2::exvGettext(const char* str)
functions.description: Translates the input string using the gettext framework and returns the translated message string. Implementation details are hidden by this wrapper.
requirements: str must be a non-null, null-terminated string.
The returned pointer refers to internal storage managed by the i18n framework; do not free it. Lifetime may be until the next translation call depending on implementation.

functions.name: Exiv2::parseInt64
functions.signature: Exiv2API int64_t Exiv2::parseInt64(const std::string& s, bool& ok)
functions.description: Parses s into a 64-bit signed integer. Also accepts text for float, Rational, and boolean values and converts them to an int64_t per library rules. Sets ok to true on success, false on failure.
requirements: s must contain a supported textual representation of an integer, float, rational, or boolean; exact accepted formats beyond the brief note are library-defined.
ok is set to indicate success; the function returns a value regardless of ok (caller must check ok).

functions.name: Exiv2::parseUint32
functions.signature: Exiv2API uint32_t Exiv2::parseUint32(const std::string& s, bool& ok)
functions.description: Parses s into a 32-bit unsigned integer. Also accepts text for float, Rational, and boolean values and converts them to a uint32_t per library rules. Sets ok to true on success, false on failure.
requirements: s must contain a supported textual representation of a uint32_t, float, rational, or boolean; exact accepted formats are library-defined.
Caller must check ok to determine if the returned value is valid.

functions.name: Exiv2::parseFloat
functions.signature: Exiv2API float Exiv2::parseFloat(const std::string& s, bool& ok)
functions.description: Parses s into a float. Also accepts text for long, Rational, and boolean values and converts them to a float per library rules. Sets ok to true on success, false on failure.
requirements: s must contain a supported textual representation of a float, long, rational, or boolean; exact accepted formats are library-defined.
Caller must check ok to determine if the returned value is valid.

functions.name: Exiv2::parseRational
functions.signature: Exiv2API Exiv2::Rational Exiv2::parseRational(const std::string& s, bool& ok)
functions.description: Parses s into a signed Rational. Also accepts text for long, float, and boolean values and converts them per library rules. If the string parses as a float, floatToRationalCast is used. Sets ok to true on success, false on failure.
requirements: s must contain a supported textual representation of a rational, long, float, or boolean; exact accepted formats are library-defined.
Caller must check ok to determine if the returned value is valid.

functions.name: Exiv2::floatToRationalCast
functions.description: Converts a float to a Rational using a very simple conversion approach. Intended for approximate representation; verify it meets your precision needs.
requirements: f may be any float; behavior for NaN/Inf is unspecified.

functions.name: Exiv2::stringTo
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
T Exiv2::stringTo(const std::string& s, bool& ok)
functions.description: Generic template function that converts a string to a value of type T using operator>> for T. Sets ok to true if the entire string parses successfully (no trailing non-whitespace), otherwise false.
requirements: T must be default-constructible and have operator>>(std::istream&, T&) defined to parse from streams.
s must contain a textual representation recognized by T’s input operator.
Caller must check ok to determine if the returned value is valid.

functions.name: Exiv2::BasicIo::~BasicIo
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the BasicIo interface. Ensures derived classes are properly destroyed via a Base pointer. Typical usage: hold and delete via BasicIo::UniquePtr or references.
requirements: Object must have been constructed; safe to destroy even if not opened or already closed.

functions.name: Exiv2::BasicIo::open
functions.description: Open the IO source using the default access mode (should allow reading and writing). Can also be used to reopen, which flushes unwritten data and resets position to start. Implemented by subclasses.
requirements: Must be implemented by the subclass.
Return 0 on success; nonzero on failure.
Reopen semantics: should flush unwritten data and reset position.

functions.name: Exiv2::BasicIo::close
functions.description: Close the IO source, flushing any unwritten data. Safe to call on an already-closed instance. After closing, the object cannot be read or written.
requirements: Must be implemented by the subclass.
Return 0 on success; nonzero on failure.
Caller should not perform I/O on this object after close succeeds.

functions.name: Exiv2::BasicIo::write
functions.signature: virtual size_t write(const byte* data, size_t wcount) = 0;
functions.description: Write a buffer to the IO source at the current position; advances by bytes written.
requirements: data must point to at least wcount bytes.
Return the number of bytes successfully written; return 0 on failure.

functions.name: Exiv2::BasicIo::putb
functions.description: Write a single byte to the IO source; advances position by one.
requirements: On success, returns the value of the byte written; on failure, returns EOF.

functions.name: Exiv2::BasicIo::read
functions.description: Read up to rcount bytes from the IO source into a newly returned DataBuf; advances by bytes read.
requirements: rcount is the maximum bytes to read and may be partially satisfied.
On failure, returned DataBuf::size_ will be 0.

functions.name: Exiv2::BasicIo::readOrThrow
functions.signature: void readOrThrow(byte* buf, size_t rcount, ErrorCode err = ErrorCode::kerCorruptedMetadata);
functions.description: Safe wrapper around read(buf, rcount) that throws an Error with the given code if the read was unsuccessful.
requirements: buf must point to at least rcount bytes.
Throws on unsuccessful read using the provided error code.

functions.name: Exiv2::BasicIo::getb
functions.description: Read one byte from the IO source; advances position by one.
requirements: On success, returns the byte value; on failure, returns EOF.

functions.name: Exiv2::BasicIo::transfer
functions.description: Remove all data from this IO source, then transfer the entire contents from src into this object. Invalidates src. Intended for use with temporary() workflows.
requirements: src must be a valid BasicIo; after return, src is invalidated and must not be used.
May throw Error on failure.

functions.name: Exiv2::BasicIo::seek
functions.signature: virtual int seek(int64_t offset, Position pos) = 0;
functions.description: Move the current IO position relative to pos (beg, cur, end) by offset bytes.
requirements: Return 0 on success; nonzero on failure.
Valid ranges for offset/pos are implementation-defined and may fail if out of bounds.

functions.name: Exiv2::BasicIo::seekOrThrow
functions.signature: void seekOrThrow(int64_t offset, Position pos, ErrorCode err);
functions.description: Safe wrapper around seek(offset, pos) that throws an Error with the provided code if the seek failed.
requirements: Caller supplies a meaningful ErrorCode for diagnostics.
Throws if seek() does not return success.

functions.name: Exiv2::BasicIo::mmap
functions.description: Provide direct access to the underlying data (e.g., file mapping or memory buffer). If writeable, changes may need munmap() to flush.
requirements: Must be implemented by the subclass.
If isWriteable is true, mapped area should be writeable.
May throw Error on failure.
Returned pointer remains valid only while the object exists and mapping is active.

functions.name: Exiv2::BasicIo::munmap
functions.description: Remove a mapping established with mmap(); if writeable, ensures changes are written back.
requirements: Return 0 on success; nonzero on failure.
Must be paired with a preceding successful mmap() when mapping is active.

functions.name: Exiv2::BasicIo::tell
functions.description: Get current IO position as offset from start.
requirements: Must be implemented by the subclass.
Return current position; semantics of failure are implementation-defined.

functions.name: Exiv2::BasicIo::size
functions.description: Get total size of the IO source in bytes.
requirements: Return size in bytes; on failure, returns (size_t)-1 as per documentation.

functions.name: Exiv2::BasicIo::isopen
functions.description: Return whether the IO source is open.
requirements: Must be implemented by the subclass.

functions.name: Exiv2::BasicIo::error
functions.description: Return 0 if the IO source is in a valid state, nonzero otherwise.
requirements: Must be implemented by the subclass.

functions.name: Exiv2::BasicIo::eof
functions.description: Return true if the IO position has reached end-of-file/stream.
requirements: Must be implemented by the subclass.

functions.name: Exiv2::BasicIo::path
functions.signature: [[nodiscard]] virtual const std::string& path() const noexcept = 0;
functions.description: Return a string identifying the IO resource (e.g., file path or URL). Useful for diagnostics.
requirements: Must be implemented by the subclass.
Returned reference must remain valid for the lifetime of the object.

functions.name: Exiv2::BasicIo::populateFakeData
functions.description: Mark all bNone blocks to bKnow to avoid allocating memory for non-metadata/pixel data. Intended after relevant metadata have been fetched into memory (for remote sources).
requirements: Should be called only after metadata are fully downloaded to memory (per note).
Semantics are implementation-defined by the subclass.

functions.name: Exiv2::IoCloser::~IoCloser
functions.description: Destructor that ensures the referenced BasicIo is closed. Useful for RAII-style scope-based closing.
requirements: Safe to destroy multiple times; close() is safe on already-closed BasicIo.

functions.name: Exiv2::IoCloser::close
functions.description: Close the referenced BasicIo if it is open.
requirements: Requires a valid BasicIo reference from construction.
Idempotent: safe to call if already closed.

functions.name: Exiv2::FileIo::FileIo
functions.description: Construct a FileIo bound to the specified file path. Does not open the file.
requirements: path must identify a file path accessible to the process when opening later.
Construction never opens nor fails.

functions.name: Exiv2::FileIo::~FileIo
functions.description: Destructor that flushes and closes an open file.
requirements: Safe if file already closed.

functions.name: Exiv2::FileIo::open
functions.description: Open the file with the specified mode (as per C fopen). Reopen flushes unwritten data and resets position. Tested primarily in binary mode.
requirements: mode must be a valid fopen-compatible mode string (e.g., "rb", "wb+").
Return 0 on success; nonzero on failure.

functions.name: Exiv2::FileIo::close
functions.description: Flush buffered writes and close the file. Safe to call if already closed.
requirements: Return 0 on success; nonzero on failure.

functions.name: Exiv2::FileIo::write
functions.signature: size_t write(const byte* data, size_t wcount) override;
functions.description: Write a buffer to the file at the current position; advances by bytes written.
requirements: File must be open for writing.
data must point to at least wcount bytes.
Returns number of bytes written; 0 on failure.

functions.name: Exiv2::FileIo::putb
functions.description: Write one byte to the file; advances by one.
requirements: File must be open for writing.
Returns byte value on success; EOF on failure.

functions.name: Exiv2::FileIo::read
functions.description: Read up to rcount bytes from the file into a DataBuf; advances by bytes read.
requirements: File must be open for reading.
On failure, returned DataBuf::size_ is 0.

functions.name: Exiv2::FileIo::getb
functions.description: Read one byte from the file; advances by one.
requirements: File must be open for reading.
Returns byte value on success; EOF on failure.

functions.name: Exiv2::FileIo::transfer
functions.description: Replace file contents with those from src. If src is a FileIo, operation may be optimized (e.g., rename). Invalidates src. Used with BasicIo::temporary().
requirements: Caller must have permission to write target; otherwise an exception is raised and src is deleted (per note).
On success, src is invalidated and must not be used.
May throw Error on failure.

functions.name: Exiv2::FileIo::seek
functions.signature: int seek(int64_t offset, Position pos) override;
functions.description: Move file position by offset relative to pos (beg, cur, end).
requirements: File must be open.
Return 0 on success; nonzero on failure.

functions.name: Exiv2::FileIo::mmap
functions.description: Map the file into the process address space. Pointer valid only while FileIo exists. If writeable, changes may not persist until munmap().
requirements: File must be open before mmap().
May throw Error on failure.
If writeable mapping used, call munmap() to ensure changes are written back.
Pointer validity tied to the FileIo lifetime and active mapping.

functions.name: Exiv2::FileIo::munmap
functions.description: Unmap a previously mapped file; if writeable, ensures changes are written back.
requirements: Return 0 on success; nonzero on failure.
Should only be called after a successful mmap().

functions.name: Exiv2::FileIo::setPath
functions.description: Close the current file (if open) and set a new path for subsequent operations.
requirements: Further opens will use the new path.
May affect internal state; ensure file is not in use elsewhere.

functions.name: Exiv2::FileIo::tell
functions.description: Return current file position offset from start.
requirements: File should be open for meaningful results.

functions.name: Exiv2::FileIo::size
functions.description: Flush buffered writes and return current file size in bytes; returns (size_t)-1 on failure.
requirements: File should be accessible and, if open for writing, buffers will be flushed before size is determined.

functions.name: Exiv2::FileIo::isopen
functions.description: Return true if the file is open.

functions.name: Exiv2::FileIo::error
functions.description: Return 0 if the file is in a valid state; nonzero otherwise.

functions.name: Exiv2::FileIo::eof
functions.description: Return true if the file position has reached EOF.

functions.name: Exiv2::FileIo::path
functions.signature: [[nodiscard]] const std::string& path() const noexcept override;
functions.description: Return the current file path.
requirements: Returned reference remains valid for the object's lifetime.

functions.name: Exiv2::FileIo::populateFakeData

functions.name: Exiv2::XmpProperties::nsDesc

functions.name: Exiv2::XmpProperties::propertyList

functions.name: Exiv2::urlencode

functions.name: Exiv2::base64encode
functions.signature: int Exiv2::base64encode(const void* data_buf, size_t dataLength, char* result, size_t resultSize)
functions.description: Encode binary data to Base64. Writes the Base64 text into the caller-provided result buffer. Returns 1 on success. The documentation states result should be NULL if it fails, but since result is an input/output pointer provided by the caller, that note is ambiguous—callers should rely on the return value to detect failure.
requirements: data_buf must point to at least dataLength bytes of readable memory.
result must point to a writable buffer of size at least ((dataLength + 2) / 3) * 4 + 1 bytes (per documentation).
resultSize must be the size of the result buffer in bytes and must be >= ((dataLength + 2) / 3) * 4 + 1.
On success, the function returns 1; callers should check the return value to detect failure.
Behavior if result is nullptr or resultSize is too small is not documented and may lead to failure or undefined behavior; callers must provide a valid buffer meeting the documented size requirement.

functions.name: Exiv2::base64decode
functions.signature: size_t Exiv2::base64decode(const char* in, char* out, size_t out_size)
functions.description: Decode Base64-encoded text from in into binary data written to out. Returns the size in bytes of the decoded output. Documentation claims -1 is returned on failure, which cannot be represented directly by size_t; if implemented as (size_t)-1, callers must treat that value as an error.
requirements: in must point to a NUL-terminated C-string containing Base64 text (format specifics not otherwise documented).
out must point to a writable buffer of at least out_size bytes.

out_size must be sufficient to hold the decoded data; if too small, decoding may fail. The exact minimum required size is not specified; callers should ensure out_size is at least (length(in) / 4) * 3.
Callers must check the return value: treat (size_t)-1 as failure if the implementation uses that sentinel as documented.

functions.name: Exiv2::TiffImage::printStructure
functions.signature: void Exiv2::TiffImage::printStructure(std::ostream& out, Exiv2::PrintStructureOption option, size_t depth)
functions.description: Prints a human-readable representation of the TIFF file structure to the provided output stream. Intended primarily as a debugging aid (like exiv2 -pS or -pR). May throw if the file cannot be read or does not look like a valid TIFF of the specific type. Not thread safe.
requirements: out must be a valid output stream ready for writing.
option selects the structure-printing mode (PrintStructureOption); valid values depend on the library’s enum.
depth controls the recursion/indent depth; must be a non-negative size_t.
This function is not thread safe; avoid concurrent calls or concurrent modification of the same image.
May throw an Error if reading fails or the image data is not valid.

functions.name: Exiv2::TiffImage::setComment
functions.description: Not supported for TIFF images because the TIFF format does not contain a comment field. Calling this will throw an Error(ErrorCode::kerInvalidSettingForImage).
requirements: Do not call for TIFF images if you expect success; this function always throws for this format.
Callers must be prepared to catch the thrown Error(ErrorCode::kerInvalidSettingForImage).

functions.name: Exiv2::TiffImage::mimeType
functions.description: Returns the MIME type string of the TIFF image (e.g., the type corresponding to TIFF).
requirements: No special requirements. Callable on a const TiffImage.

functions.name: Exiv2::TiffImage::pixelWidth
functions.description: Returns the width in pixels of the primary image in the TIFF.
requirements: No special requirements. Callable on a const TiffImage.
If the primary image width is not available, the return may be 0 (based on the default-initialized cache).

functions.name: Exiv2::TiffImage::pixelHeight
functions.description: Returns the height in pixels of the primary image in the TIFF.
requirements: No special requirements. Callable on a const TiffImage.
If the primary image height is not available, the return may be 0 (based on the default-initialized cache).

functions.name: Exiv2::TiffParser::decode
functions.signature: static Exiv2::ByteOrder Exiv2::TiffParser::decode(Exiv2::ExifData& exifData, Exiv2::IptcData& iptcData, Exiv2::XmpData& xmpData, const Exiv2::byte* pData, size_t size)
functions.description: Decodes metadata from a memory buffer containing TIFF-formatted data into the provided Exif, IPTC, and XMP containers. Returns the byte order used by the data. No format validation checks are performed on input.
requirements: pData must be non-null and point to a buffer of at least size bytes containing data in TIFF format; no validation is performed.
size must be the exact length of the buffer to decode.
exifData, iptcData, and xmpData must be valid containers; their contents may be replaced/updated by the decode operation.

functions.name: Exiv2::TiffParser::encode
functions.signature: static Exiv2::WriteMethod Exiv2::TiffParser::encode(Exiv2::BasicIo& io, const Exiv2::byte* pData, size_t size, Exiv2::ByteOrder byteOrder, Exiv2::ExifData& exifData, const Exiv2::IptcData& iptcData, const Exiv2::XmpData& xmpData)
functions.description: Encodes the provided metadata into TIFF format, attempting non-intrusive in-place update of the original image data buffer first and falling back to intrusive rewrite to the given IO. Returns which write method was used. If all metadata containers are empty, returns wmIntrusive and writes nothing (no TIFF header) to io.
requirements: io must be a valid BasicIo; it is used only when intrusive writing is required. It must be writable in that case.
pData must be non-null and point to a buffer of at least size bytes containing a TIFF binary image. It may be modified if non-intrusive writing is possible.
size must match the length of the pData buffer.
byteOrder specifies the byte order to use for encoding.
exifData is supplied by non-const reference and may be modified by the encoder as part of write processing.
iptcData and xmpData are read-only inputs to the encoder.
If the return value is wmIntrusive, a new TIFF structure is written to io; the original memory block pData,size may be partially updated and should not be used anymore.
If there is no metadata to encode (all containers empty), the function returns wmIntrusive and writes nothing to io.

functions.name: Exiv2::newTiffInstance
functions.description: Factory function that creates and returns a new TiffImage wrapped in Image::UniquePtr. The caller takes ownership of the returned object.
requirements: io must own a valid Exiv2::BasicIo; ownership is transferred to the new image and the caller must not use the BasicIo after passing it. Use Image::io() to access it temporarily.
If create is true, a new image is created and any existing data is overwritten; otherwise an existing TIFF is opened.
Caller receives an owning UniquePtr and is responsible for object lifetime.

functions.name: Exiv2::isTiffType
functions.description: Checks whether the data accessible through the provided BasicIo appears to be a TIFF image.
requirements: iIo must reference readable data containing the start of a candidate image stream.
Behavior of the advance parameter is not documented here; any effect on the IO position is unknown from this header and should be confirmed against implementation or higher-level docs.

functions.name: Exiv2::Jp2Image::Jp2Image
functions.description: Constructs a JPEG-2000 (JP2) image object bound to the provided BasicIo. The constructor cannot report status directly; callers must check good() after construction to determine success or failure. The BasicIo ownership is transferred to the image; use Image::io() to obtain a temporary reference if needed.
requirements: Caller must pass a std::unique_ptr<Exiv2::BasicIo>; ownership is transferred to the Jp2Image instance.
After construction, the caller should check good() to verify the image opened/initialized successfully.
Callers must not continue using the BasicIo instance after passing it to the constructor; use Image::io() for temporary access.
The create flag specifies behavior: false to read an existing image; true to create a new file.

functions.name: Exiv2::Jp2Image::readMetadata
functions.description: Reads metadata from the underlying JP2 image into the Jp2Image object. Overrides Image::readMetadata(). Intended to parse and populate metadata structures for subsequent access.
requirements: The associated BasicIo must provide readable image data.
The image object should be in a good() state before calling.
Errors are reported via exceptions of type Error (inferred from library patterns); callers should be prepared to handle exceptions.

functions.name: Exiv2::Jp2Image::writeMetadata
functions.description: Writes buffered metadata from the Jp2Image object back to the underlying JP2 image. Overrides Image::writeMetadata(). Internally delegates to an implementation that writes to a BasicIo and may validate image data.
requirements: The underlying BasicIo must be writable (inferred from function purpose and accompanying doWriteMetadata documentation).
The image data must be valid; otherwise an Error may be thrown (per doWriteMetadata comment).
Callers should handle exceptions on I/O errors or invalid image data.

functions.name: Exiv2::Jp2Image::printStructure
functions.signature: void Exiv2::Jp2Image::printStructure(std::ostream& out, Exiv2::PrintStructureOption option, size_t depth)
functions.description: Prints the structure of the image file for debugging (e.g., as used by exiv2 -pS). Not thread-safe. Throws on read failures or if the data does not resemble the expected JP2 format.
requirements: This function is not thread-safe; callers must ensure no concurrent use that could cause races.
Caller must provide a valid std::ostream reference for output.
May throw Error if reading fails or the data is not valid; callers should be prepared to handle exceptions.
Depth should be a non-negative size_t; large values may produce extensive output (inferred from parameter semantics).

functions.name: Exiv2::Jp2Image::setComment
functions.description: Setting a user comment is not supported for JP2 images. Calling this function will throw Error(ErrorCode::kerInvalidSettingForImage).
requirements: Do not call for JP2; any call will throw an Error with ErrorCode::kerInvalidSettingForImage.
Callers must be prepared to handle the thrown exception.

functions.name: Exiv2::Jp2Image::mimeType
functions.description: Returns the MIME type string for JP2 images. Marked [[nodiscard]] to encourage callers to use the return value.
requirements: None beyond having a valid Jp2Image instance; function is const and does not throw per declaration (no explicit exception spec).
Callers should use the return value ([[nodiscard]]).

functions.name: Exiv2::newJp2Instance
functions.description: Factory function that creates and returns a new Jp2Image instance as an Image::UniquePtr. Ownership of the created object is transferred to the caller via the unique pointer; the BasicIo ownership is transferred into the created image.
requirements: Caller must pass a std::unique_ptr<Exiv2::BasicIo>; ownership is transferred to the created image.
The caller becomes responsible for the returned Image::UniquePtr and its lifetime.
The create flag determines whether to read an existing image (false) or create a new file (true).
Callers should check the returned image’s good() to determine success after construction (inferred from constructor documentation).

functions.name: Exiv2::isJp2Type
functions.description: Checks whether the data accessible via the provided BasicIo represents a JPEG-2000 (JP2) image. Returns true if the file is recognized as JP2.
requirements: Caller must provide a valid Exiv2::BasicIo reference with readable data.

Behavior of the 'advance' flag is not documented here; based on its name it likely controls whether the I/O position is advanced during probing (inferred). Callers should ensure their code tolerates possible position changes or reset the I/O position as needed.
Function returns a boolean; callers should not assume it throws on non-JP2 data (behavior not specified).

functions.name: Exiv2::PsdImage::PsdImage
functions.description: Constructor that opens a Photoshop (PSD) image using a BasicIo for reading/writing metadata. Purpose: establish an Image backed by the provided I/O object. Usage: construct with a BasicIo you no longer need to use directly; then immediately check good() to confirm successful initialization. Note: ownership of the BasicIo is transferred to the PsdImage; use Image::io() to obtain a temporary reference afterward.
requirements: Caller must pass a std::unique_ptr<Exiv2::BasicIo>; ownership is transferred to the PsdImage and the caller must not use the BasicIo after passing it.
Caller should check good() on the constructed object to determine success or failure.
To access the underlying I/O after construction, use Image::io() to get a temporary reference.
Whether a null unique_ptr is permitted is unknown from this header.

functions.name: Exiv2::PsdImage::readMetadata
functions.description: Reads and parses metadata from the underlying PSD image into the object’s metadata containers. Typical usage is to call this after successful construction and before accessing Exif/Iptc/XMP data.
requirements: The PsdImage instance should be in a good() state before calling (inferred from constructor documentation and common Image usage).
Underlying BasicIo must provide readable PSD data (implied by function purpose).
Error and exception behavior is not specified here; callers should be prepared for errors if the image is invalid or I/O fails (inferred from library patterns).

functions.name: Exiv2::PsdImage::writeMetadata
functions.description: Writes buffered metadata back to the PSD image. Internally uses doWriteMetadata to emit metadata; intended after modifying metadata on the Image instance.
requirements: The PsdImage instance should be in a good() state and reference valid PSD data (inferred).
May throw an Error on I/O errors or invalid image data (noted in doWriteMetadata comment). Callers must be prepared to handle exceptions.
Caller should ensure any metadata to be written has been prepared on the Image (e.g., ExifData/IptcData/XmpData) before calling (inferred).

functions.name: Exiv2::PsdImage::setComment
functions.description: Not supported for PSD images. Calling this function will throw an Error(ErrorCode::kerInvalidSettingForImage). Use other metadata containers if you need to store descriptive text.
requirements: Do not call for PSD images unless you are prepared to handle an exception.
Callers must catch and handle Error(ErrorCode::kerInvalidSettingForImage).

functions.name: Exiv2::PsdImage::mimeType
functions.description: Returns the MIME type for Photoshop images. The value returned is "image/x-photoshop". Note: Although the official type is "image/vnd.adobe.photoshop", historical platform behavior (e.g., macOS 10.4.8) mapped it differently.
requirements: None beyond having a valid PsdImage instance.

functions.name: Exiv2::newPsdInstance
functions.description: Factory function that creates a new PsdImage and returns it as an owning pointer (Image::UniquePtr). Purpose: convenient construction while transferring ownership of the BasicIo. The caller owns the returned object, and the smart pointer ensures deletion.
requirements: Caller must pass a std::unique_ptr<Exiv2::BasicIo>; ownership is transferred to the created image.
Caller assumes ownership of the returned Image::UniquePtr and its lifetime.
The meaning of the 'create' flag (e.g., creating a new file vs. opening existing) is not documented here; behavior is unknown.

functions.name: Exiv2::isPsdType
functions.description: Returns true if the provided BasicIo appears to contain a Photoshop (PSD) image. Intended to probe the I/O source to detect file type. The 'advance' parameter likely controls whether the I/O position is advanced during probing, but exact semantics are not specified here.
requirements: Caller must provide a valid Exiv2::BasicIo referencing readable data.
Effect of 'advance' on the stream position is not specified in this header; callers should not rely on the I/O position remaining unchanged unless verified in implementation/documentation.
The expected initial position within the stream (e.g., beginning) is not specified; ensure iIo is positioned appropriately for type detection (inferred).

functions.name: Exiv2::PgfImage::PgfImage
functions.description: Constructor to open an existing PGF image or create a new one. Ownership of the provided BasicIo is transferred to the PgfImage. Because constructors cannot report errors directly, callers must check Image::good() after construction to verify success. Pass create=false to open/read an existing PGF; pass create=true to create a new image file (overwriting any existing data).
requirements: io must be a valid, heap-allocated Exiv2::BasicIo wrapped in std::unique_ptr; ownership is transferred and the caller must not use the BasicIo after passing it.
If create is true, any existing data at the target will be overwritten (caller must be prepared for data loss).
Call Image::good() after construction to verify the object is usable; handle failure paths accordingly.
The underlying BasicIo must be readable (for open) and/or writable (for create) as appropriate.

functions.name: Exiv2::PgfImage::readMetadata
functions.description: Reads metadata from the associated PGF image into the Image object. Intended to parse supported metadata (Exif and IPTC) from the current BasicIo source.
requirements: The PgfImage instance must have been constructed with a valid Exiv2::BasicIo and represent a PGF image (or be in a readable state).
Must be called when the underlying BasicIo is positioned/available for reading; any required seeking is handled internally.
Callers should be prepared to handle exceptions or error states if the I/O fails or the image is invalid (inferred from overall design).

functions.name: Exiv2::PgfImage::writeMetadata
functions.description: Writes buffered metadata for the PGF image back to the underlying BasicIo target. Implementation delegates to an internal routine that may throw on I/O errors or invalid image data.
requirements: The PgfImage must have a writable BasicIo and represent a valid PGF image target.
Buffered metadata to be written should be prepared/updated on the Image before calling.
Callers must handle potential exceptions on I/O errors or invalid image data (inferred from doWriteMetadata() documentation).

functions.name: Exiv2::PgfImage::mimeType
functions.description: Returns the MIME type string for PGF images. For PgfImage it always returns "image/pgf". [[nodiscard]] suggests callers should use the return value.
requirements: None; callable on a valid PgfImage instance at any time.
Callers should not ignore the returned value (as indicated by [[nodiscard]]).

functions.name: Exiv2::newPgfInstance
functions.description: Factory function that creates and returns a new PgfImage wrapped in Image::UniquePtr. Ownership of the provided BasicIo is transferred to the new image. The returned smart pointer owns the image and will delete it when destroyed.
requirements: io must be a valid, heap-allocated Exiv2::BasicIo wrapped in std::unique_ptr; ownership is transferred and the caller must not use the BasicIo after passing it.
The caller assumes ownership of the returned Image::UniquePtr and must keep it alive as needed.
If create is true, the target will be created and any existing data may be overwritten.
Call Image::good() on the returned object to verify successful construction.

functions.name: Exiv2::isPgfType
functions.description: Checks whether the data accessible via the given BasicIo represents a PGF image. Returns true if the PGF format is detected, otherwise false. The advance flag typically indicates whether the function may advance the I/O position during probing (behavior inferred from common library patterns; exact semantics not documented here).
requirements: iIo must be readable and positioned such that detection bytes can be examined (commonly at the beginning of the file).

If advance is true, callers should expect the I/O position may change during detection; if false, callers may rely on the position remaining unchanged (inferred; exact behavior not explicitly documented).
Callers should handle a false result without assuming any I/O state changes.

functions.name: Exiv2::EpsImage::EpsImage
functions.description: Constructs an EPS image object bound to the provided BasicIo. The constructor does not report errors directly; callers should check good() after construction to verify the image was opened/created successfully. The BasicIo ownership is transferred to the EpsImage and should no longer be used by the caller; use Image::io() to access it indirectly. The create flag selects opening an existing image (false) or creating a new one (true).
requirements: io must be a valid pointer to a BasicIo instance; ownership is transferred to EpsImage and must not be used by the caller after passing it in.
Call good() on the constructed object to determine whether initialization/opening succeeded.
Use Image::io() to obtain a temporary reference to the underlying BasicIo if needed after construction.
The create parameter controls behavior: false to read an existing image; true to create a new file.

functions.name: Exiv2::EpsImage::readMetadata
functions.description: Reads metadata from the associated EPS image into the EpsImage object. Intended to be called after construction to populate image/exif/iptc/xmp fields as supported for EPS.
requirements: The EpsImage instance must have been constructed with a valid BasicIo.
The underlying BasicIo must provide readable EPS data.
Callers should expect this function to throw on I/O or format errors (exact error types are library-defined; not specified here).

functions.name: Exiv2::EpsImage::writeMetadata
functions.description: Writes the metadata currently stored in the EpsImage object back to the underlying EPS file/stream, updating supported sections.
requirements: The EpsImage must have been constructed with a valid BasicIo.
The underlying BasicIo/target must be writable when persisting changes.
Callers should expect this function to throw on I/O or format errors (exact error types are library-defined; not specified here).

functions.name: Exiv2::EpsImage::setComment
functions.description: Not supported for EPS images. Calling this function will throw an instance of Error(ErrorCode::kerInvalidSettingForImage). Do not use to set comments on EPS.
requirements: Do not rely on this function to succeed; it always throws.
Callers must handle the exception Error(ErrorCode::kerInvalidSettingForImage).

functions.name: Exiv2::EpsImage::mimeType
functions.description: Returns the MIME type string for EPS images. Exact value is library-defined (e.g., a PostScript/EPS MIME), but not specified in this header.
requirements: None beyond having a valid EpsImage instance.

functions.name: Exiv2::newEpsInstance
functions.description: Factory function that constructs and returns a new EpsImage wrapped in an Image::UniquePtr. Ownership of the provided BasicIo transfers to the created image. The caller owns the returned UniquePtr, which ensures deletion.
requirements: io must be a valid pointer to a BasicIo; ownership is transferred and the caller must not use it after passing it in.
The caller should check image->good() on the returned instance to verify success.
The create parameter selects opening an existing image (false) or creating a new file (true).

functions.name: Exiv2::isEpsType
functions.description: Checks whether the data accessible via iIo represents an EPS image. The advance flag influences probing behavior (implementation-specific; not documented here). Returns true if EPS is detected, false otherwise.
requirements: iIo must reference a valid, readable data source.
Behavior of the advance parameter is not documented in this header; callers should consult implementation/docs or assume stream position may change depending on its value.

functions.name: Exiv2::MrwImage::MrwImage
functions.description: Constructs an MRW image handler that either opens an existing MRW file (create == false) or creates a new image (create == true). Ownership of the provided BasicIo is transferred to the MrwImage. Callers must check good() after construction to verify the object initialized successfully. When creating a new image, any existing data in the target is overwritten.
requirements: io must be a valid, non-null std::unique_ptr to an Exiv2::BasicIo instance.
Ownership of the BasicIo is transferred; callers must not use the BasicIo object after passing it to the constructor. Use Image::io() to obtain a temporary reference if needed.
Call good() after construction to determine success or failure.
If create is false, the underlying IO must refer to an existing MRW image readable by the library.
If create is true, the underlying IO must be writable; any existing data may be overwritten.

functions.name: Exiv2::MrwImage::readMetadata
functions.description: Reads metadata from the MRW image. Exif is supported directly; IPTC is read from Exif if present. Populates the Image’s metadata containers.
requirements: The object should be in a good state (good() == true) prior to calling.
Underlying BasicIo must be readable and positioned appropriately for reading the image headers/metadata.
The source must be a valid MRW image; behavior is unspecified for non-MRW content.

functions.name: Exiv2::MrwImage::writeMetadata
functions.description: Not implemented for MRW. Calling this will throw an Error(ErrorCode::kerWritingImageFormatUnsupported). Use this class for reading MRW metadata only.
requirements: Callers must not rely on this function to succeed.
Callers must be prepared to handle an exception of type Error with code ErrorCode::kerWritingImageFormatUnsupported.

functions.name: Exiv2::MrwImage::setExifData
functions.description: Not supported for MRW because writing is not implemented. Calling this will throw an Error(ErrorCode::kerInvalidSettingForImage).
requirements: Callers must be prepared to handle an exception of type Error with code ErrorCode::kerInvalidSettingForImage.
Do not expect any metadata to be modified as a result of this call.

functions.name: Exiv2::MrwImage::setIptcData
functions.description: Not supported for MRW because writing is not implemented. Calling this will throw an Error(ErrorCode::kerInvalidSettingForImage).
requirements: Callers must be prepared to handle an exception of type Error with code ErrorCode::kerInvalidSettingForImage.
Do not expect any metadata to be modified as a result of this call.

functions.name: Exiv2::MrwImage::setComment
functions.description: Not supported; MRW format does not contain a comment. Calling this will throw an Error(ErrorCode::kerInvalidSettingForImage).
requirements: Callers must be prepared to handle an exception of type Error with code ErrorCode::kerInvalidSettingForImage.
Do not expect any comment to be stored for MRW images.

functions.name: Exiv2::MrwImage::mimeType
functions.description: Returns the MIME type string for MRW images. Typical usage is to query the content type for I/O or HTTP purposes. Exact return value not specified in this header.
requirements: None beyond a valid MrwImage instance; function is const and does not modify state.

functions.name: Exiv2::MrwImage::pixelWidth
functions.description: Returns the pixel width of the MRW image. Intended to be used after metadata has been read.

Returns a 32-bit unsigned integer; behavior if metadata was not read is unspecified in this header.

functions.name: Exiv2::MrwImage::pixelHeight
functions.description: Returns the pixel height of the MRW image. Intended to be used after metadata has been read.
requirements: Call readMetadata() before calling to ensure dimensions are available (inferred from common Image API usage; not explicitly stated here).
Returns a 32-bit unsigned integer; behavior if metadata was not read is unspecified in this header.

functions.name: Exiv2::newMrwInstance
functions.description: Factory function that creates a new MrwImage and returns an owning Image::UniquePtr to it. The returned smart pointer ensures the image object will be deleted when it goes out of scope.
requirements: io must be a valid, non-null std::unique_ptr to an Exiv2::BasicIo instance.
Ownership of the BasicIo is transferred to the created image; do not use the BasicIo object after passing it. Use Image::io() to get a temporary reference if needed.
If create is false, io should reference an existing MRW image; if true, io must be writable and any existing data may be overwritten.
Call good() on the returned Image to verify successful construction before further use.

functions.name: Exiv2::isMrwType
functions.description: Checks whether the data accessible via iIo is an MRW image. Optionally advances the I/O position depending on the advance flag. Useful for type detection before constructing an image object.
requirements: iIo must be readable; it should be positioned such that type detection can inspect the necessary header bytes (typically at the beginning of the file; exact position not specified here).

functions.name: Exiv2::CrwImage::CrwImage
functions.description: Constructs a CRW image object that either opens an existing Canon CRW image or prepares a new one. Ownership of the provided BasicIo is transferred to the image. Callers should check good() after construction to confirm success. Use Image::io() to access the internal I/O object temporarily.
requirements: io must be a valid std::unique_ptr to an initialized Exiv2::BasicIo instance; ownership is transferred to the CrwImage on construction.
After passing io to this constructor, the caller must not use the BasicIo instance directly; use Image::io() to obtain a temporary reference if needed.
Set create to false to open/read an existing CRW image; set to true to create a new image file (any existing data may be overwritten).
Call good() after construction to verify that the image was opened/created successfully.

functions.name: Exiv2::CrwImage::readMetadata
functions.description: Reads metadata from the associated CRW image source into the CrwImage instance. For CRW, only Exif metadata and a comment are supported; IPTC is not present in CRW.
requirements: The CrwImage must have been constructed with a valid BasicIo and should reference CRW image data.
May throw on I/O or parsing errors (error behavior not detailed here).
Only Exif and comment data are expected to be populated; IPTC is not supported for CRW.

functions.name: Exiv2::CrwImage::writeMetadata
functions.description: Writes the in-memory metadata of the CrwImage back to the underlying CRW image. For CRW, only Exif metadata and a comment are applicable.
requirements: The CrwImage must be associated with a writable BasicIo if metadata is to be written.
Only Exif and comment metadata are supported for CRW; IPTC is not present.
May throw on I/O or encoding errors (exact error types not detailed here).

functions.name: Exiv2::CrwImage::setIptcData
functions.description: Not supported for CRW images. Attempting to set IPTC metadata on a CRW image will throw an exception (Error(ErrorCode::kerInvalidSettingForImage)).
requirements: Do not call this function for CRW images; CRW does not contain IPTC metadata.
If called, the function will throw Error(ErrorCode::kerInvalidSettingForImage); callers must be prepared to handle this exception.

functions.name: Exiv2::CrwImage::mimeType
functions.description: Returns the MIME type string for Canon CRW images. Intended for identifying the media type of this image.
requirements: None beyond having a valid CrwImage instance. Return value content is implementation-defined but represents the CRW MIME type.

functions.name: Exiv2::CrwImage::pixelWidth
functions.description: Returns the pixel width of the CRW image as a 32-bit unsigned integer.

functions.name: Exiv2::CrwImage::pixelHeight
functions.description: Returns the pixel height of the CRW image as a 32-bit unsigned integer.
requirements: A valid CrwImage instance is required. The height may be unknown if the image/metadata has not been read; behavior in that case is implementation-defined.

functions.name: Exiv2::CrwParser::decode

functions.name: Exiv2::CrwParser::encode

requirements: blob must be a valid buffer container (output) that will receive the encoded binary image.
pData must be a non-null pointer to data in CRW format; no format checks are performed before encoding.
size must be the length in bytes of the buffer pointed to by pData.
pCrwImage must be a valid, non-null pointer to the source CrwImage containing metadata to encode.
Throws Error if the metadata cannot be encoded; callers must handle exceptions.

functions.name: Exiv2::newCrwInstance
functions.description: Factory function that creates and returns a new CrwImage instance owned by a smart pointer. The returned Image::UniquePtr owns the image and will delete it automatically.
requirements: io must be a valid std::unique_ptr to an initialized Exiv2::BasicIo; ownership is transferred to the new image.
After passing io, the caller must not use the BasicIo directly; use Image::io() on the returned image to access it temporarily.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces a byte stream that the fuzzing harness will split into
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR() values and an unsigned int for how many regex filters to use.
# The target stub uses up to 4 regex patterns (ECMAScript, std::regex). We provide
# a compact, seeded set of valid, interesting regex patterns to explore different
# engine features without causing regex_error.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

BASIC_LITERALS = [
    "exiv", "image", "meta", "Exif", "IPTC", "XMP", "JPEG", "TIFF",
    "ICC", "width", "height", "mime", "preview", "tag", "value",
]

CHAR_CLASSES = [
    r"[A-Za-z]+", r"[0-9]+", r"[\w-]+", r"[[:alpha:]]+", r"[[:digit:]]+",
    r"[A-Fa-f0-9]{2,8}", r"[\x00-\x7F]", r"[^\s]",
]

QUANTIFIERS = ["?", "*", "+", "{1,3}", "{2,5}"]

GROUPS = [
    r"(Exif|IPTC|XMP)", r"(jpeg|jpg|png)", r"(tiff|tif)", r"(width|height)",
]

ANCHORS = ["^", "$", "\b", "\B", "\A", "\Z"]

LOOKAROUNDS = [
    r"(?=meta)", r"(?!deprecated)", r"(?i)",  # (?i) inline case-insensitive
]

ESCAPES = [r"\.", r"\+", r"\*", r"\?", r"\|", r"\[", r"\]", r"\(", r"\)", r"\{", r"\}"]

# A pool of pre-validated complex patterns to avoid regex_error
PREVALID = [
    r"^Exiv2\\b",
    r"mime(Type)?",
    r"(Exif|IPTC|XMP):?\\s*",
    r"width\\s*[:=]\\s*[0-9]{1,5}",
    r"height\\s*[:=]\\s*[0-9]{1,5}",
    r"\\b(tag|name|group|desc)\\b",
    r"(?i)jpeg|png|tiff",
    r"^xmp(Packet|Data)$",
    r"ICC(Profile)?",
    r"^([A-Fa-f0-9]{2}:){3,7}[A-Fa-f0-9]{2}$",
    r"preview(Width|Height)?",
    r"^((?!deprecated).)*$",
]

def rand_choice(rng: random.Random, arr: List[str]) -> str:
    return arr[rng.randrange(len(arr))]

def build_pattern(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Construct a safe, moderately complex ECMAScript regex.
    parts: List[str] = []
    # Randomly choose to start with an anchor or inline flag
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(rand_choice(rng, ANCHORS))
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        parts.append(rand_choice(rng, LOOKAROUNDS))
    # Build a sequence of 3-6 atoms
    atoms_cnt = rng.randint(3, 6)
    for _ in range(atoms_cnt):
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.20:
            atom = rand_choice(rng, BASIC_LITERALS)
        elif choice < 0.40:
            atom = rand_choice(rng, CHAR_CLASSES)
        elif choice < 0.60:
            atom = rand_choice(rng, GROUPS)
        elif choice < 0.75:
            atom = rand_choice(rng, ESCAPES)
        else:
            atom = rand_choice(rng, BASIC_LITERALS)
        # Maybe apply a quantifier (avoid overlarge for performance)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            atom = f"{atom}{rand_choice(rng, QUANTIFIERS)}"
        # Maybe insert alternation by grouping safely
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            alt = rand_choice(rng, BASIC_LITERALS + ["exiv2", "data", "info"])  # safe alts
            atom = f"({atom}|{alt})"
        parts.append(atom)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(rand_choice(rng, ANCHORS))
    pat = "".join(parts)
    # Truncate to <= 64 characters as the stub will do
    return pat[:64]

def encode_records(records: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Encode patterns as null-terminated strings to ease parsing by the harness if it expects C-strings
    # but in general FUZZ_PARAM_STR reads raw slices; we include length-prefixed framing to be generic.
    # Format: [count:1][len:2][bytes] repeated. Count will be determined by harness via modulo; but
    # we include all for richness. The consumer will slice strings from this buffer.
    out = bytearray()
    # Write a simple header magic to help any consumers seeking structure
    out += b"RXG0"  # magic
    out.append(len(records) & 0xFF)
    for s in records:
        b = s.encode('utf-8')
        if len(b) > 64:
            b = b[:64]
        out += len(b).to_bytes(2, 'little')
        out += b
    return bytes(out)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Decide how many regexes to provide (the stub uses up to 4)
    n = rng.randint(0, 4)
    patterns: List[str] = []

    # Mix prevalidated patterns and constructed ones
    # Ensure all are valid and not too long
    for _ in range(n):
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            patterns.append(rand_choice(rng, PREVALID))
        else:
            patterns.append(build_pattern(rng))

    # To enrich the buffer for additional FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls (if any), append extras up to 8
    extras = rng.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(extras):
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            patterns.append(rand_choice(rng, PREVALID))
        else:
            patterns.append(build_pattern(rng))

    buf = encode_records(patterns)
    if len(buf) > MAX_TOTAL:
        buf = buf[:MAX_TOTAL]
    return buf

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target: Generate interesting plain-text strings that are valid for many Exiv2 fuzz stubs.
# Strategy:
# - Produce short ASCII identifiers (for prefixes, properties, keys).
# - Include XML/XMP-like packets for XmpParser::encode paths.
# - Include EXIF date/time strings, rational strings, numeric tokens.
# - Include URL-like strings and percent-encoded forms for Uri/encoding helpers.
# - Include regex-friendly snippets for dumpLibraryInfo without catastrophic backtracking.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Single bytes payload used by FUZZ_PARAM_STR; return as bytes.

SAFE_ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
SAFE_IDENT = SAFE_ALNUM + "_:-"


def _rand_identifier(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=12, charset=SAFE_ALNUM) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(charset) for _ in range(n))
    # ensure starts with alpha when needed
    if charset is SAFE_ALNUM and not s[0].isalpha():
        s = 'a' + s[1:]
    return s


def _rand_prefix(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = _rand_identifier(rng, 2, 8, charset=string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits)
    return ''.join(ch for ch in base if ch.isalnum())


def _rand_property(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return _rand_identifier(rng, 3, 16, charset=SAFE_IDENT)


def _rand_xml_text(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    words = [
        "alpha", "beta", "gamma", "delta", "title", "description", "creator",
        "camera", "lens", "subject", "keywords", "copyright"
    ]
    w = rng.choice(words)
    val = _rand_identifier(rng, 3, 12, charset=string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " -_")
    return f"<{w}>{val}</{w}>"


def _rand_xmp_packet(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Minimal valid-ish XMP packet that Exiv2 can accept; small and well-formed.
    title = _rand_identifier(rng, 3, 12, charset=string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-")
    desc = _rand_identifier(rng, 5, 20, charset=string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-")
    return (
        "<?xpacket begin=\"\ufeff\" id=\"W5M0MpCehiHzreSzNTczkc9d\"?>\n"
        "<x:xmpmeta xmlns:x=\"adobe:ns:meta/\">\n"
        " <rdf:RDF xmlns:rdf=\"http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#\""
        "           xmlns:dc=\"http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/\""
        "           xmlns:xmp=\"http://ns.adobe.com/xap/1.0/\">\n"
        f"  <rdf:Description dc:title=\"{title}\" xmp:CreatorTool=\"gen\">{_rand_xml_text(rng)}</rdf:Description>\n"
        " </rdf:RDF>\n"
        "</x:xmpmeta>\n"
        "<?xpacket end=\"w\"?>"
    )


def _rand_exif_datetime(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    y = rng.randint(1970, 2169)
    m = rng.randint(1, 12)
    d = rng.randint(1, 28)
    H = rng.randint(0, 23)
    M = rng.randint(0, 59)
    S = rng.randint(0, 59)
    return f"{y:04d}:{m:02d}:{d:02d} {H:02d}:{M:02d}:{S:02d}"


def _rand_iso_date(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    y = rng.randint(1900, 2199)
    m = rng.randint(1, 12)
    d = rng.randint(1, 28)
    return f"{y:04d}{m:02d}{d:02d}"


def _rand_iso_time(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    h = rng.randint(0, 23)
    m = rng.randint(0, 59)
    s = rng.randint(0, 59)
    tz_h = rng.randint(-12, 12)
    tz_m = rng.choice([0, 15, 30, 45])
    sign = '-' if tz_h < 0 else '+'
    tz_h = abs(tz_h)
    return f"{h:02d}{m:02d}{s:02d}{sign}{tz_h:02d}{tz_m:02d}"


def _rand_rational(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    a = rng.randint(-100000, 100000)
    b = rng.randint(1, 100000)
    return f"{a}/{b}"


def _rand_number(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # mix signed, unsigned, and float
    choose = rng.randint(0, 2)
    if choose == 0:
        return str(rng.randint(-2**31, 2**31 - 1))
    elif choose == 1:
        return str(rng.randint(0, 2**32 - 1))
    else:
        return f"{rng.uniform(-1e6, 1e6):.6f}"


def _rand_url(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    schemes = ["http", "https", "file", "ftp", "sftp", "data"]
    scheme = rng.choice(schemes)
    host = _rand_identifier(rng, 3, 10, charset=string.ascii_lowercase) + ".example.com"
    path = "/" + _rand_identifier(rng, 3, 8, charset=SAFE_ALNUM)
    qs = "q=" + _rand_identifier(rng, 3, 8, charset=SAFE_ALNUM)
    if scheme == "file":
        return f"file://{path}"
    if scheme == "data":
        return "data:text/plain;base64,SGVsbG8="
    return f"{scheme}://{host}{path}?{qs}"


def _percent_encode(s: str) -> str:
    out = []
    for ch in s:
        o = ord(ch)
        if (65 <= o <= 90) or (97 <= o <= 122) or (48 <= o <= 57) or ch in "-_.~":
            out.append(ch)
        else:
            out.append("%" + format(o, "02X"))
    return ''.join(out)


def _rand_percent_encoded(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(string.printable[:94]) for _ in range(rng.randint(4, 24)))
    return _percent_encode(s)


def _rand_regex(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Compose simple, safe regex (avoid catastrophic backtracking): literals and character classes
    tokens = [
        r"[A-Za-z0-9_]+",
        r"[A-Fa-f0-9]{2,8}",
        r"title|subject|description",
        r"dc\.[A-Za-z_]+",
        r"xmp\.[A-Za-z_]+",
    ]
    parts = [rng.choice(tokens) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3))]
    return '^' + '.*'.join(parts) + '$'


def _lines_join(parts: List[str]) -> str:
    return "\n".join(parts) + "\n"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Assemble multiple lines; each FUZZ_PARAM_STR call likely consumes a chunk.
    # We include several sections to feed different stubs.
    lines: List[str] = []

    # 1) XMP namespace prefix and property-friendly tokens
    for _ in range(3):
        lines.append(_rand_prefix(rng))
        lines.append(_rand_property(rng))

    # 2) Valid XMP packet snippet
    lines.append(_rand_xmp_packet(rng))

    # 3) EXIF and IPTC-friendly date/time
    lines.append(_rand_exif_datetime(rng))
    lines.append(_rand_iso_date(rng))
    lines.append(_rand_iso_time(rng))

    # 4) Numeric/rational strings
    for _ in range(3):
        lines.append(_rand_number(rng))
    lines.append(_rand_rational(rng))

    # 5) URL and percent-encoded strings for URI helpers
    for _ in range(2):
        lines.append(_rand_url(rng))
    lines.append(_rand_percent_encoded(rng))

    # 6) IPTC/XMP key-like strings
    prefixes = ["dc", "xmp", "photoshop", "exif", "tiff", _rand_prefix(rng)]
    for _ in range(3):
        p = rng.choice(prefixes)
        prop = _rand_property(rng)
        lines.append(f"Xmp.{p}.{prop}")

    # 7) Regex patterns for dumpLibraryInfo
    for _ in range(2):
        lines.append(_rand_regex(rng))

    # 8) Comment strings with optional charset header
    charset_heads = ["charset=Ascii ", "charset=Unicode ", "charset=Jis ", ""]
    body = _rand_identifier(rng, 8, 40, charset=string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.")
    lines.append(rng.choice(charset_heads) + body)

    # 9) Language alternatives prefix
    lines.append("lang=en-US " + _rand_identifier(rng, 5, 20, charset=string.ascii_letters + " -_"))

    # 10) Hex-like strings for isHex
    hexpart = ''.join(rng.choice('0123456789abcdef') for _ in range(rng.randint(4, 16)))
    lines.append(hexpart)

    # 11) Filenames or simple tokens for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME fallbacks
    lines.append("test.bin")

    # 12) Misc small payloads
    lines.extend([
        "title",
        "CreatorTool",
        "subject",
        "keywords",
        "description",
    ])

    payload = _lines_join(lines)
    # Enforce size limit
    if len(payload) > 4096:
        payload = payload[:4096]
    return payload.encode("utf-8", errors="replace")

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for raw binary data buffers tailored to Exiv2 fuzz stubs expecting:
# - ICC profile appends (valid-ish ICC headers)
# - Image file signatures (JPEG/PNG/EXV/PSD/GIF/JP2/WebP/TIFF/CRW/CR2/ORF/RW2/RAF/ASF/QuickTime/MKV/RIFF)
# - IPTC IIM4 blocks inside Photoshop IRB
# - Base64 roundtrips
# - Generic typed reads (short/long/rational/float/double)
# - Small random payloads for BasicIo::write
# Sizes kept <= 4096.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

# Helpers to build specific small, valid-ish chunks

def icc_profile(min_len: int = 128, max_len: int = 1024, rnd: random.Random = None) -> bytes:
    r = rnd or random
    size = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    size = max(128, size)
    # Construct 128-byte header; use separate pack pieces to avoid tuple count mismatch
    hdr = bytearray(128)
    # size (u32)
    struct.pack_into(">I", hdr, 0, size)
    # preferred CMM
    struct.pack_into(">4s", hdr, 4, b"lcms")
    # version
    struct.pack_into(">I", hdr, 8, 0x04300000)
    # deviceClass, colorSpace, PCS
    struct.pack_into(">4s4s4s", hdr, 12, b"mntr", b"RGB ", b"XYZ ")
    # dateTime (12 bytes ASCII)
    struct.pack_into("12s", hdr, 24, b"202501011200")
    # signature 'acsp'
    struct.pack_into("4s", hdr, 36, b"acsp")
    # platform
    struct.pack_into("4s", hdr, 40, b"APPL")
    # flags
    struct.pack_into(">I", hdr, 44, 0)
    # manufacturer, model
    struct.pack_into("4s4s", hdr, 48, b"APPL", b"    ")
    # attributes (8)
    struct.pack_into(">Q", hdr, 56, 0)
    # rendering intent
    struct.pack_into(">I", hdr, 64, 1)
    # illuminant XYZ (3x 16.16)
    struct.pack_into(">III", hdr, 68, 0x0000F6D6, 0x00010000, 0x0000D32D)
    # creator
    struct.pack_into("4s", hdr, 80, b"pyic")
    # profileID (16 bytes)
    struct.pack_into("16s", hdr, 84, b"\x00" * 16)
    # reserved (28)
    struct.pack_into("28s", hdr, 100, b"\x00" * 28)

    # Tag table: 1 tag 'desc' placed immediately after the 12-byte table
    remaining = size - 128
    if remaining < 12:
        remaining = 12
        size = 128 + remaining
        struct.pack_into(">I", hdr, 0, size)
    tag_table = bytearray()
    tag_table += struct.pack(">I", 1)
    tag_offset = 128 + 12
    tag_data = b"This is an ICC profile created for testing."
    pad = (4 - (len(tag_data) % 4)) % 4
    tag_size = len(tag_data) + pad
    tag_table += b"desc" + struct.pack(">II", tag_offset, tag_size)
    blob = bytes(hdr) + bytes(tag_table) + tag_data + (b"\x00" * pad)
    if len(blob) < size:
        blob += os.urandom(size - len(blob))
    return blob[:max_len]


def png_minimal(rnd: random.Random = None) -> bytes:
    r = rnd or random
    sig = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"
    width = r.randint(16, 256)
    height = r.randint(16, 256)
    ihdr_data = struct.pack(
        ">IIBBBBB",
        width,
        height,
        8,  # bit depth
        2,  # color type RGB
        0, 0, 0,
    )
    def crc32(b: bytes) -> int:
        import zlib
        return zlib.crc32(b) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    ihdr = struct.pack(">I", 13) + b"IHDR" + ihdr_data + struct.pack(">I", crc32(b"IHDR" + ihdr_data))
    iend = struct.pack(">I", 0) + b"IEND" + b"" + struct.pack(">I", crc32(b"IEND"))
    return sig + ihdr + iend


def jpeg_minimal(rnd: random.Random = None) -> bytes:
    return (
        b"\xff\xd8\xff\xe0\x00\x10JFIF\x00\x01\x01\x00\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00\x00"
        b"\xff\xdb\x00C\x00" + bytes([
            16,11,12,14,12,10,16,14,13,14,18,17,16,19,24,40,26,24,22,22,24,49,35,37,29,40,58,51,61,60,57,51,56,55,64,72,92,78,64,68,87,69,55,56,80,109,81,87,95,98,103,104,103,62,77,113,121,112,100,120,92,101,103,99
        ]) +
        b"\xff\xc0\x00\x11\x08\x00\x10\x00\x10\x01\x01\x11\x00"
        b"\xff\xc4\x00\x14\x00\x00\x01\x05\x01\x01\x01\x01\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x01\x02\x03\x04\x05\x06\x07\x08\t\n\x0b"

def exv_minimal() -> bytes:
    return b"\xff\x01Exiv2\xff\xd9"


def psd_header(rnd: random.Random = None) -> bytes:
    r = rnd or random

def gif_header(rnd: random.Random = None) -> bytes:

    w = r.randint(16, 64)
    h = r.randint(16, 64)

def jp2_minimal() -> bytes:
    sig = b"\x00\x00\x00\x0cjP  \r\n\x87\n"
    brand = b"jp2 "
    minor = 0
    compat = b"jp2 "
    ftyp = struct.pack(">I4s4sI4s", 24, b"ftyp", brand, minor, compat)
    return sig + ftyp


def webp_minimal() -> bytes:

    size = len(payload)
    return b"RIFF" + struct.pack("<I", size) + payload


def tiff_minimal(rnd: random.Random = None) -> bytes:
    hdr = b"II" + struct.pack("<H", 42) + struct.pack("<I", 8)
